prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Draw a corrected TRUE BACK walking sprite source for the EXACT SAME intermediate-armored character in Images1/2. Image1 fixes costume, materials, gait and identity; Image2 fixes native body stature and rear costume. ONLY the rear ARM/HAND CARRY POSE must be corrected. Output FOUR columns by TWO rows: eight SEPARATE COMPLETE TRUE BACK figures on genuine transparency. Row1: neutral back stand, first-foot contact, recoil, passing. Row2: same neutral back stand, opposite-foot contact, recoil, passing. No frontal figure, face, eyes, copied frontal chest or front kneecaps. Equal physical scale and stable foot baseline. Leave at least 25 source pixels of empty gutter between complete bodies. Keep every head, boot, sleeve and arm entirely inside its cell.
Critical correction: the old backs have frontal-style lowered fists and weapons seem to lie on the backs of the hands. Reposition BOTH lower arms in a natural LOW FORWARD CARRY, relative to the direction the character is facing (away from viewer). Elbows remain low and just outside the flanks. The lower forearms turn slightly FORWARD, AWAY FROM THE CAMERA, toward the front/sides of the pelvis. Distal wrists and empty gripping hands are therefore partly occluded BY THE HIPS/THIGH SIDES and appear foreshortened from this rear view. Show the rear/outer surfaces of the armored forearms, not front-facing palms or visible curled fingertips. Thumbs wrap on the far/front side of the future handle; the backs/outer knuckles remain anatomically correct from the rear. The future independent weapons will be drawn IN FRONT OF THE WEARER and BEHIND the rear-view body/arms. This is NOT a hands-behind-back pose: do not bring hands together over the small of the back. Keep a small lateral separation for two independent one-handed weapons, one per hand; never join the wrists or adopt a rifle/two-handed grip. No elbow raised sideways, pointing, aiming, blade, gun, placeholder object, handle or prop painted into the body source. Hands EMPTY.
Preserve head/hair or raised garment hood, exact armor rank, every original garment length, colors, rear armor design, anatomical asymmetries, mechanical arm if any, proportions and boots of Images1/2. Do not invent armor, bare skin, backpack or ornaments. The whole body, shoulder, elbow, wrist and feet must follow the back perspective coherently, with a quiet whole-figure gait and tiny torso bob. Do not mirror front arms, graft strips or leave floating fragments. Keep compact matte native64 game finish, restrained outline and consistent upper-left light. Background completely transparent; no labels, text, grid, scenery or ground shadow.
